newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rates mixed, demand stronger.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rates mixed, demand stronger.

text.p: Croatian money market rates were mixed on Wednesday amid slightly stronger demand as commercial bank accounts shrank again, dealers said.
"The banking sector liquidity has worsened once again after Tuesday's temporary recovery," one dealer said.
Only two banks had relatively small shortfalls to square through market borrowings in overnight trade on Tuesday, the dealer said.
Fresh trade was put at 21.2 million kuna by noon, with borrowers seeking another 12 million kuna, which they were not likely to get after exceeding debt limits set by creditors.
The banks were also busy repaying Lombard funds to the central bank in expectation of money for pension payments from the state pension fund, an official said.
Total volume of outstanding Lombard loans shrank to 108 million kuna from 145 million at the end of Tuesday.
More than two thirds of the money market settlements were call money loans, granted at a regular 10.5 percent. One bank agreed to pay a higher rate of 11 percent to secure a new loan.

One 30-day loan was made at 17 percent, also higher than usual. But two foreign banks loaned each other seven-day funds at 8.2 percent, compared with 11-12 recently. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
